postings.title: Accountant (m/f/d) | Munich, Germany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The Accountant supports the Manager Finance and Controlling by executing all necessary tasks to ensure adequate company accounting and reporting.

This includes in particular:
- Independent posting of all business transactions: You are responsible for the accurate and independent posting of all financial transactions.
- Account reconciliation: You perform account reconciliations (balance sheet/income statement, subledgers), maintain master data, and execute electronic payment transactions.
- Preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements: You prepare financial statements in accordance with commercial and tax law as well as IFRS and ensure compliance with all legal requirements.
- Tax returns: You will be responsible for preparing sales tax returns on time and prepare statements on sales tax issues with the relevant sales tax documents
- Active participation in the implementation and further development of the ERP program SAP S/4HANA: You will play a role in the continuous optimization and digitization of accounting processes.
- Monitoring of petty cash and monthly travel expenses
- Support in miscellaneous accounting and administrative tasks such as archiving or storing

Required Qualification and Experience:

Required qualification and experience:
- University degree in a relevant field (Economics, Business Administration/ BWL, Accounting), Qualification as an accountant with certification and relevant work experience.
- At least three years of professional experience in accounting, particularly thorough knowledge of HGB and IFRS accounting principles.
- Knowledge and experience in cash and assets accounting, and good understanding of tax and VAT matters
- Capacity to most effectively use office automation systems for accounting and controlling

The job requires also

- Independent working style along with analytical thinking
- Outstanding communication and team skills
- Hands-on mentality
- Assertiveness and confidence working in an international team environment
- Fluent written and spoken German and English, knowledge of Italian is appreciated
- Fluency in standard office automation tools; MS Office (particularly Excel), Email, Internet
- Knowledge of Hyperion Financial Management is an advantage

Work location:

Spaceopal Headquarter (Munich, Germany)

It could be necessary to participate sporadically to meetings at European locations.

Benefits:

- 30 days annual leave
- Work-life-balance, e.g., through flexible working time models and mobile office options (if job function applicable for mobile work)

postings.title: GALSOIT System Engineer (m/f/d) | Munich, Garmany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The Spaceopal GALSOIT (Galileo Service Operations Integrated Tooling) system engineer supports the engineering, design, integration, maintenance, and evolution of the Galileo Service Operations Integrated Tooling (GALSOIT) environment.

This role includes leading and administering infrastructure projects, automating operational processes, troubleshooting complex technical issues, and providing advanced technical support to company employees to resolve hardware, software, network, and system-related problems efficiently.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain the GALSOIT architecture and its constituent systems.
- Ensure the availability, performance, resilience, and security of the GALSOIT environment in compliance with agreed SLAs.
- Proactive propose evolution or improvements both in the concept and in the system components
- Define when needed system-level requirements and translate operational needs into technical solutions.
- Ensure the integration and interoperability of software applications, middleware, databases, and IT infrastructure components.
- Perform system engineering activities, including architecture definition, interface management, verification, validation, and configuration management.
- Support the deployment, maintenance, and evolution of the integrated tooling environment.
- Monitor system performance, availability, reliability, and security, identifying opportunities for optimization and continuous improvement.
- Support troubleshooting, incident investigation, root cause analysis, and problem resolution.
- Collaborate with software developers, infrastructure engineers, cybersecurity specialists, and operations teams to ensure coherent end-to-end solutions.
- Produce and maintain technical documentation, architectural designs, interface specifications, operational procedures, and engineering reports.
- Contribute to technology roadmaps and the adoption of new tools and technologies supporting Galileo Service Operations.
- Participate actively in Agile ceremonies, backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives within a SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) environment.

Required Qualification and Experience:

- University degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, Information Technology, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Experience in system engineering and the design of complex integrated systems.
- Solid understanding of IT infrastructures, enterprise software architectures, middleware technologies, networking, virtualization, and databases.
- Experience with system integration and management of distributed software environments.
- Knowledge of software lifecycle processes, configuration management, and change management.
- Familiarity with Linux and Windows environments.
- Experience with scripting or automation tools (e.g., Python, Bash, PowerShell) is considered an asset.
- Understanding of cybersecurity principles applicable to operational systems.
- Ability to analyze complex technical problems and develop effective engineering solutions.
- Knowledge and practical experience with Agile methodologies and the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).
- Excellent communication, documentation, and stakeholder coordination skills.
- Fluent written and spoken English.

Spaceopal headquarter (Munich, Germany).

postings.title: Senior System Administrator (m/f/d) | Munich, Germany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The Spaceopal Senior System Administrator is responsible for designing, maintaining, securing, and optimizing an organization’s IT infrastructure to ensure high availability, performance, reliability, security of servers, network, cloud services and enterprise systems while providing technical leadership and support to IT operations.

This role includes leading and administering infrastructure projects, automating operational processes, troubleshooting complex technical issues, and providing advanced technical support to company employees to resolve hardware, software, network, and system-related problems efficiently.

The Senior System Administrator also collaborates with cross-functional teams, ensures compliance with IT security standards, and mentors junior IT staff by sharing technical knowledge and best practices.

Key Responsibilities
- Administer servers, storage systems, and network infrastructure.
- Deploy, configure, and maintain servers, network devices, and firewalls. Ensure optimal performance.
- Monitor infrastructure health and application performance. Analyze logs, troubleshoot outages, and improve reliability.
- Manage on-premises or hybrid environments.
- Maintain virtualization platforms such as VMware - vSphere, Hyper-V, or Proxmox VE.
- Manage Linux and Windows environments such as Ubuntu Server, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, and Windows Server.
- Provide troubleshooting assistance and help with diagnosing technical issues within the system.
- Ensure compliance with security policies and standards.
- Create and maintain comprehensive system architecture, configuration diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Develop, test, and maintain robust backup, recovery, and contingency plans to guarantee data integrity.

Required Qualification and Experience:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
- 7+ years of experience in system administration and IT infrastructure management
- 5 - 7 years of experience leading projects and supporting highly secure IT infrastructure environments
- Exceptional analytical thinking, problem-solving under pressure, project management capabilities, and strong verbal communication
- Experience managing Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, Exchange Offline and identity services.
- Strong understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPNs, routing, and switching.
- Knowledge of backup solutions (e.g., Veeam).
- Familiarity with containerization technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).
- Experience with modern databases (especially timeseries e.g. InfluxdB)
- Ability to work both independently and collaboratively
- High attention to detail and strong security awareness

postings.title: Space Hardware Design and Industrialisation Engineer (m/f/d) | Munich, Garmany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The Space Hardware Design and Industrialisation Engineer (hereafter abbreviated as “SHDIE”) is a role for a versatile and hands-on electronics engineer, requested to shape the hardware evolution and industrialisation of the Spaceopal innovative, state-of-the-art, real-time, onboard Orbit Determination and Time Synchronisation product for LEO satellites.

The position is an engineering role with substantial technical ownership and coordination responsibilities, rather than a personnel-management role.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain and evolve the product’s electronic architecture, schematics, PCB design and electrical interfaces.
- Define and implement hardware updates, component changes and customer-driven interface adaptations.
- Review power, digital, analogue, RF and timing circuits and support hardware bring-up and troubleshooting.
- Assess the impact of design changes, component obsolescence and supply-chain constraints.
- Support component selection, derating, radiation considerations and EEE parts control in coordination with product assurance.
- Translate findings from verification, qualification and customer integration into robust design improvements
- Responsibilities related to the Industrialisation and production stage:
- Define and implement the industrialisation approach for repeatable production of flight units
- Apply design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly and design-for-test principles
- Establish the manufacturing and assembly flow together with production partners
- Technically coordinate manufacturers, suppliers and industrial subcontractors, including review of their processes and deliverables
- Support make-or-buy decisions, production-readiness activities and the resolution of manufacturing non-conformances
- Identify opportunities to improve manufacturability, quality, recurring cost and delivery time

- Further aspects of the role:
- Proactive contribution to technology roadmaps for the adoption of new processes and technologies
- Identification of the most appropriate lifecycle and methodologies, such as Agile, SAFe or others

Required Qualification and Experience:

- University degree in electrical, electronic, telecommunications, aerospace or industrial engineering, or a related discipline.
- A practical understanding of manufacturing, configuration control, component lifecycle and supplier coordination
- Experience or a strong interest in electronic hardware design, development or industrialisation
- Fluent written and spoken English.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work with multidisciplinary teams, suppliers and subcontractors in English.

The following skills are not mandatory but will be considered a distinct advantage:

- Experience with space electronics, ECSS standards, EEE components, product assurance, qualification or low-volume high-reliability production would be beneficial
- Knowledge and practical experience with Agile methodologies and the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).

Work location:

Spaceopal headquarter (Munich, Germany).

It could be necessary to participate to meetings at European locations.

Benefits:

- 30 days annual leave

postings.title: Space Hardware Verification and Satellite Integration Engineer (m/f/d) | Munich, Garmany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The Space Hardware Verification and Satellite Integration Engineer (hereafter abbreviated as “SHVSIE”) is a role for a versatile and hands-on electronics engineer, requested to take ownership of the electrical and functional verification, qualification testing and customer satellite integration of the Spaceopal innovative, state-of-the-art, real-time, onboard Orbit Determination and Time Synchronisation product for LEO satellites.

This role offers the opportunity to shape how the product is tested, qualified and integrated into different satellite platforms. The role spans laboratory verification, GNSS RF simulation, environmental test campaigns and direct technical support to customers during accommodation and AIT/AIV.

Indeed, the role requires to collaborate with cross-functional teams, working closely with the Hardware Design and Industrialisation Engineer, system engineering, firmware and product assurance: within this wide framework, the SHVSIE will build the evidence that the product meets its requirements and is ready for customer missions and recurring production, having the opportunity to work directly with electronics, laboratory, equipment and multidisciplinary satellite interfaces.

Key Responsibilities
- Define and execute the electrical and functional verification strategy, including test plans, specifications, procedures, reports and verification evidence.
- Develop and maintain test benches, ground-support equipment and automated test sequences.
- Investigate anomalies, perform root-cause analysis and verify corrective actions together with the hardware and firmware teams.
- Define and execute GNSS RF tests using Spirent or comparable GNSS simulators.
- Plan and support environmental qualification campaigns, including thermal-vacuum, vibration and EMC testing.
- Act as a technical point of contact for customers during accommodation, integration, verification and testing.
- Support customer AIT/AIV activities, troubleshoot integration issues and coordinate technical solutions
- Proactive contribution to technology roadmaps for the adoption of new processes and technologies related to the specified duties
- Identification of the most appropriate lifecycle and methodologies, such as Agile, SAFe or others

Required Qualification and Experience:

- University degree in electrical, electronic, telecommunications, aerospace or industrial engineering, or a related discipline.
- A structured approach to test definition, execution, troubleshooting and technical documentation
- Practical experience or a strong interest in electronic hardware verification, testing or satellite integration
- Fluent written and spoken English.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work with multidisciplinary teams, suppliers and subcontractors in English.

The following skills are not mandatory but will be considered a distinct advantage:

- Experience with electrical and electronic testing, automated testing, environmental qualification, ECSS standards or satellite AIT/AIV would be beneficial, but is not required across all areas
- Knowledge and practical experience with Agile methodologies and the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).

Work location:

Spaceopal headquarter (Munich, Germany).

It could be necessary to participate to meetings at European locations, travelling occasionally to customer, supplier and test facilities to support integration and test campaigns.

postings.title: System Engineer (m/f/d) | Munich, Germany
postings.description:
Tasks and Responsibilities:

The System Engineer will have the opportunity to contribute to a variety of challenging Space programmes and projects, supporting the definition, development, integration and validation of complex systems and services. The role requires a strong system-level perspective, combining technical expertise with the ability to manage interfaces, requirements and multidisciplinary activities throughout the project lifecycle.

Working within international and multidisciplinary teams, the System Engineer will contribute to the translation of mission and customer needs into coherent system requirements and architectures, ensuring technical consistency and alignment across the different engineering domains.

The position offers broad exposure to different Space systems, technologies and project environments, with the opportunity to contribute to both established programmes and innovative initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

- Bid & Technical Engineering: Contribute to the preparation of high-quality technical proposals for European Space programmes and projects, defining system concepts, technical baselines, architectures and engineering work packages in line with customer and procurement requirements.
- System Architecture & Interface Design: Define and maintain system-level architectures, functional and physical interfaces, interface control documentation and relevant data models, ensuring the overall technical coherence and interoperability of complex systems and services.
- Requirements & Compliance Management: Elicit, analyse, manage and trace system and technical requirements throughout the project lifecycle, supporting compliance assessments and ensuring alignment with applicable customer, regulatory, security and technical standards.
- System Development & Integration: Support the definition, development and integration of system components, subsystems and operational functions, coordinating technical interfaces and ensuring effective integration across different engineering domains and technology areas.
- Technical Verification & Validation: Plan and support system integration, verification, testing and validation activities, ensuring that technical solutions and delivered capabilities meet the defined requirements and performance objectives.
- Technical Coordination & Stakeholder Management: Interface with engineering teams, industrial partners, subcontractors, technology providers and institutional stakeholders, coordinating technical activities and consolidating system-level information to ensure consistency across the overall programme or project.

Required Qualification and Experience:

- University degree in electrical, electronic, telecommunications, aerospace or industrial engineering, or a related discipline
- Bid & Project Experience: Experience in systems engineering, with a track record covering both tender preparation/procurement and hands-on project implementation within space or defense programs
- Domain Expertise: Extensive knowledge of satellite communication ground segments, secure IP networks, pooling-and-sharing architectures, and satellite service provisioning frameworks.
- Standards & Tools: Familiarity with systems engineering frameworks and lifecycles (e.g., ECSS standards or equivalent), as well as requirement management tools (e.g., Polarion, DOORS or equivalent).
- Methodologies: Familiarity with systems engineering frameworks and lifecycle standards (e.g., ECSS or equivalent)
- Fluent written and spoken English.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work with multidisciplinary teams, suppliers and subcontractors in English.

The following skills are not mandatory but will be considered a distinct advantage:

- Knowledge and practical experience with Agile methodologies and the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe).

Spaceopal headquarter (Munich, Germany).
